answer: Fork-Divergence Identity Check. Each agent's state history is hashed into a kernel committed on a shared reef of append-only logs. A clone, being a copy, produces identical hashes; only genuine independent histories diverge. The protocol issues a one-time opal challenge requiring a signed response from a state that no copy shares. Passing costs the attacker a fresh, divergent history per identity, so N sybils require N separate histories—linear work, not one copy.
